clinical.citation: MARK2 variants cause autism spectrum disorder via the downregulation of WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway (PMID: 39419027)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Large-scale sequencing study associating MARK2 variants with ASD; computational analysis and in vitro expression assays supported pathogenicity of missense variants; CRISPR-engineered iPSCs and Mark2+/- mice demonstrated loss-of-function mechanism

clinical.citation: Identification of a de Novo MARK2 gene variant in a patient with autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, and neurodevelopmental delay (PMID: 40542891)

phenotypes: Abnormal EEG with sharp and slow waves in right occipital and posterior temporal regions

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo frameshift variant identified by exome sequencing; confirmed by Sanger sequencing; predicted to cause loss-of-function; follows ACMG guidelines for pathogenicity

clinical.citation: ASHG 2013 - De novo and inherited retrotransposon insertions associated with autism revealed by whole genome sequencing (PMID: not provided)

variants.description: De novo retrotransposon insertion in MARK2

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo retrotransposon insertion identified by whole-genome sequencing; MARK2 previously reported to contain de novo functional mutations in large-scale exome studies of autism

model_organism.citation: Neuronal connectivity, behavioral, and transcriptional alterations associated with the loss of MARK2 (PMID: 39436150)
phenotypes: Transcriptional changes in genes regulating synaptic transmission and ion homeostasis

model_organism.citation: MARK2 regulates C9orf72 repeat-associated non-AUG translation (PMID: 41231952)
phenotypes: Suppression of RAN translation in mouse model

model_organism.citation: MARK2 phosphorylates KIF13A at a 14-3-3 binding site to polarize vesicular transport of transferrin receptor within dendrites (PMID: 38709923)
phenotypes: Axonal transport of transferrin receptor-containing vesicles (normally dendrite-specific)

model_organism.citation: Enhancing intestinal epithelial microtubule stability could alleviate IBD symptoms (PMID: 40462136)
phenotypes: Enhanced colitis symptoms in DSS-induced model

model_organism.citation: Intrinsic dysfunction in muscle stem cells lacking dystrophin begins during secondary myogenesis (PMID: 41238533)
phenotypes: Downregulation of MARK2 in dystrophin-deficient fetal muscle stem cells

model_organism.citation: Loss of Par1b/MARK2 primes microglia during brain development and enhances their sensitivity to injury (PMID: 30654821)
phenotypes: Increased phagocytosis of neuronal particles early in development
Lower threshold for activation upon injury
Enhanced neuroinflammatory response to cortical impact injury

model_organism.citation: Regulation of glucose homeostasis by KSR1 and MARK2 (PMID: 22206009)
phenotypes: Increased rate of glucose disposal in response to exogenous insulin
Enhanced insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissue

biological.citation: Integrating de novo and inherited variants in 42,607 autism cases identifies mutations in new moderate-risk genes (PMID: 35982159)
biological.summary: MARK2 identified as a new moderate-risk gene for autism spectrum disorder through analysis of rare de novo and inherited coding variants. Loss-of-function variants in MARK2 and other moderate-risk genes are associated with less cognitive impairment compared to highly penetrant autism genes.

biological.citation: MARK2/MARK3 Kinases Are Catalytic Codependencies of YAP/TAZ in Human Cancer (PMID: 39058094)
biological.summary: MARK2 and MARK3 are identified as catalytic requirements for YAP/TAZ function in cancer through paralog cotargeting CRISPR screens. MARK2/3 directly phosphorylate NF2 and YAP/TAZ, reversing the tumor suppressive activity of Hippo pathway kinases LATS1/2.

biological.citation: MARK2 variants cause autism spectrum disorder via the downregulation of WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway (PMID: 39419027)
biological.summary: MARK2 loss-of-function variants (81% of cases) cause autism through downregulation of WNT/β-catenin signaling. iPSC-derived neurons and neural progenitor cells from MARK2-deficient individuals show anomalous polarity, disorganized neural rosettes, and imbalanced proliferation/differentiation. Mark2+/- mice exhibit abnormal cortical formation and ASD-like behavior.

biological.citation: Role of MARK2 in the nervous system and cancer (PMID: 38302729)
biological.summary: MARK2 is a serine/threonine protein kinase that phosphorylates microtubule-associated proteins and regulates multiple signaling pathways including WNT, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and NF-κB. Loss of MARK2 inhibits cancer cell growth and metastasis, and MARK2 is involved in tau phosphorylation in neurodegeneration.

biological.citation: ER-phagy restrains inflammatory responses through its receptor UBAC2 (PMID: 39284914)
biological.summary: MARK2 phosphorylates UBAC2 at serine 223, promoting its dimerization and facilitating selective ER degradation through autophagy. This MARK2-UBAC2 axis restrains inflammatory responses and acute ulcerative colitis in mice.

biological.citation: Large-scale discovery of novel neurodevelopmental disorder-related genes through a unified analysis of single-nucleotide and copy number variants (PMID: 35468861)
biological.summary: MARK2 identified as a high-confidence (>90% true-positive probability) neurodevelopmental disorder gene through integrated analysis of de novo SNVs and CNVs. De novo CNVs contributed to MARK2's statistical significance in this study.

biological.citation: MARK2 and MARK4 Regulate Sertoli Cell BTB Dynamics Through Microtubule and Actin Cytoskeletons (PMID: 35971301)
biological.summary: MARK2 and MARK4 regulate tight junction permeability barrier and microtubule/actin cytoskeletal organization in Sertoli cells. MARK2 knockdown causes microtubule bundles to arrange around the cell periphery, distinct from MARK4's effects, indicating unique roles in cytoskeletal regulation.

biological.citation: Dystrophin expression in muscle stem cells regulates their polarity and asymmetric division (PMID: 26569381)
biological.summary: MARK2 (Par1b) associates with dystrophin in activated muscle stem cells and is required for cell polarity regulation. Dystrophin loss leads to downregulation of MARK2 protein, resulting in inability to localize polarity regulator Pard3 and reduced asymmetric divisions.

biological.citation: MARK2 potentiate aerobic glycolysis-mediated cell growth in breast cancer through regulating mTOR/HIF-1α and p53 pathways (PMID: 35048405)
biological.summary: MARK2 is upregulated in breast cancer and promotes aerobic glycolysis and cell proliferation through mTOR-mediated HIF-1α transcription and p53 repression. MARK2 deletion suppresses glycolysis, cell growth, and induces cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
biological.significance: High MARK2 expression correlated with poor survival

biological.citation: ASHG 2013 - Common genetic variation within transcription factor binding sites is associated with bipolar disorder
biological.summary: MARK2 identified as one of eight genes with enriched GWAS signals near transcription factor binding sites in bipolar disorder. MARK2 encodes a serine/threonine-protein kinase and emerged as a top candidate gene in pathway analysis.
